line: Lenovo ThinkPad X1 Carbon Gen 14 Aura Edition (2026, Panther Lake)
config_name: ThinkPad X1 Carbon Gen 14 — Core Ultra X7 358H (Arc B390 12 Xe), 32GB LPDDR5, 1TB SSD, 14" 2.8K 120Hz touch OLED

specs.gpu: Intel Arc B390 (12 Xe cores) integrated

battery.notes: 58Wh; touch OLED + B390 slightly shorter runtime.

price.notes: X7/Arc B390 tier is X1 Carbon-exclusive per Ultrabookreview; CAD estimate.

reviews.quote: if you want the Core Ultra X7 hardware with the Arc B390 GPU, that's only offered on the Carbon and not on the other two
the model Lenovo sent me is actually $100 cheaper tha[n last year's]

praises: Arc B390 plays esports titles (Valorant, LoL) at 1080p medium — genuinely playable on a 1 kg ThinkPad
Touch OLED tier adds pen input support for markup
Best iGPU option in any business ultrabook this year
Same repairable Space Frame and 1 kg weight as base config
vPro on the X-series chips for fleet management
complaints: Big price jump over the Ultra 7 tier for modest gaming uplift
B390 drivers still maturing; occasional stutter in older DX11 titles
Touch glass adds weight and glare vs matte non-touch
Battery a bit shorter than the Ultra 7 OLED config

design_philosophy: The performance apex of the X1 Carbon line: Panther Lake's Arc B390 graphics only appear on this flagship, letting light gaming and GPU-accelerated work coexist with the classic 1 kg ThinkPad form.
rating_notes: Inferred from Gen 14 OLED review (CNET/Ultrabookreview): Arc B390 → +2 gaming vs 4-Xe config, −0.5 battery/thermals for higher GPU power; touch adds pen_touch 5 (touch only, no active pen); +1 creative_work for B390 media encode. Image from lenovo.com CA CDN.
